How recognition, translation and composition relate
Recognition, translation and composition can collapse into one request; cost and what stays adjustable change with it.
The OCR model reads the source lettering and bubble positions, the translation model translates it, and the composition stage produces the translated page locally or with an image model.

Setting the OCR model to \"Recognize with the translation model\", or selecting the same model for both, merges the three steps into one cheaper request. Different models run recognition, text-only translation and visual layout in sequence.

Add an image provider in AI settings and enable image editing output on its model. Native OpenAI, Gemini, Seedream, Qwen, xAI and SiliconFlow image protocols are supported. Each page segment can incur a paid request; providers are never switched automatically.

Local detection supplies numbered positions. The AI reads the original page and enlarged crops, translates, and chooses line breaks and direction. Numbered regions keep their original positions and use measured source lettering as the font baseline, shrinking on overflow. Without candidates, the AI locates text directly. Following the translation model uses one request; separate models run recognition, translation, then visual layout. AI location always uses this recognition and typesetting flow.
The AI did not return a complete usable typesetting plan. Retry translation or select on-device or cloud OCR.
Delete saved translations for this book. Settings and glossary are kept.

A non-AI engine needs a separate recognition stage: use on-device or cloud OCR, or pick a vision model for AI recognition. Whole-page edits cannot use it.
Google Translate failed, translated image not updated: %1$s
Recognition emits text blocks and coordinates; the locator decides whether a vision model or OCR handles it.

Recognition only produces text and geometry; the rest of this group chooses the path:

- **AI vision**: the whole page goes to a vision model, one request returns text and boxes without OCR, billed per image request.
- **On-device OCR**: models ship on the device, run offline and are not billed, comic build only.
- **Cloud OCR**: the image is uploaded and recognized remotely, billed per call.

Specify the source language explicitly where possible: “Auto” makes the model infer it, which misreads mixed pages more often.

Preprocessing (upscale, invert, binarize) applies to on-device OCR only and needs a retranslate to take effect.

Without an on-device runtime, saved on-device options fall back to what this build supports, and automatic translation is paused so it cannot start billed cloud recognition on its own.
The text stage translates line by line; the engine decides glossary, context and fallback behavior.

Each recognized line is translated one to one:

- **AI text model**: glossary, neighbouring dialogue and a retry budget, requires an AI key.
- **Google Translate**: one request per line to the free endpoint, no glossary or cross-balloon context, and no fallback to AI on failure.
- **Follow translation settings**: uses the global engine from Translation settings, applied from the next page.

“Combine with AI recognition” means one model does recognition and translation in a single request, so there is no separate text stage; the engine can still be switched, and choosing Google only hands the text to an external engine.

Thinking level applies to AI requests only; the retry count covers automatic retries of a failed page.
The composition stage decides how the translation is laid out and whether erasing and typesetting run locally.

Composition produces the final image:

- **Local erase and typesetting**: erase the source text, then typeset with the on-device font, no network request.
- **Cover source text and typeset**: keep the original lettering, paint over it and typeset on top.
- **AI erase, local typesetting**: an image model removes the text, typesetting stays on device, billed per image request.
- **AI redraw a region / the whole page**: a model repaints the region or the page; a whole-page redraw has no text stage.

A whole-page redraw sends only image edit requests, billed per page segment, with no recognition or translation requests.

Model-based erase engines and on-device bubble detection are comic build only; text scale applies to local typesetting only.
